conviction_note: H1 revenue, EBITDA, net debt and the cut FY27 guide (£45.0m vs £50.3m consensus) were all pre-released on 28 Oct, so the move turns on whether that guide holds after Ibstock's 2 Nov supplier warning and the 5 Nov BoE hike, on the interim dividend and on the cash-flow bridge. Those pull in opposite directions (findings sum -0.2) against a stock that has fallen another 15% since the warning with no new company information. So p_up sits at 52 and abs_move at 6.0, raised for the guidance risk, two-analyst coverage and 61% realised vol. The small gap in sign between the findings sum (-0.2) and the scaled number (+0.24) is the washed-out tape plus the name's positive reactions on its last two pre-released interims (+9.6%, +1.5%), which go into p_up and not into any finding.

findings.finding: The FY27 guide set on 28 Oct already embeds a sharp H2 decline: £45.0m FY less £25.5m H1 implies c.£19.5m H2 EBITDA, about 16-22% below the prior-year H2 depending on the SBP basis and 24% below this H1. Reiteration is therefore achievable and would read as relief against a stock that has fallen a further 15% since the warning (41.5p to 35.3p) without any new company statement.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pre-released interims: +9.64% (Nov 2024), +1.54% (Nov 2025). The 28 Oct 2026 guide cut drew -15.3% close to close.
findings.why_not_priced: Two analysts, $0.9m a day of turnover and heavy holder selling. The price has fallen 28% from 49p since 27 Oct against a 10% EBITDA guide cut, so it trades as if a further cut were coming; if the market believed the £45m it would not have kept drifting on rising volume (4.75m shares on 16 Nov).
findings.independence: FY26 final results give the prior-year H2 base (FY26 EBITDA before SBP £52.3m, H1 £28.1m): https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/brickability-group--brck/final-results/9666643

findings.finding: Brick supplier Ibstock warned on 2 Nov, after BRCK's last statement. UK brick market volumes fell 17% year on year in Jul-Aug, its clay sales in Q3 were 22% below expectations, and 'weak market conditions continued through September and October'. Forterra cut on 11 Nov. That raises the risk that BRCK's Distribution division, its main brick channel, trims the £45m guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last guidance surprise (28 Oct 2026) moved the stock -15.3%; the Apr 2026 pre-close day moved -7.8% (bid withdrawal on the same day).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: BRCK's post-warning drift began on 28 Oct and continued through Ibstock's 2 Nov update. The Jul-Aug volume decline fell inside BRCK's H1, which BRCK already reported at -1.1% revenue, so BRCK's revenue clearly does not track industry brick volumes one for one. Only the Sep-Oct weakness is new relative to BRCK's guide, and BRCK set its guide on 28 Oct already knowing its own October.
findings.independence: Forterra cut its FY EBITDA expectation to c.£50m on 11 Nov (aggregator, not the primary RNS): https://quartr.com/events/forterra-plc-fort-trading-update_oSjd6kLW

findings.finding: The BoE raised Bank Rate 25bp to 4% on 5 Nov (8-1, one vote for 50bp). BRCK told the market on 28 Oct that its Distribution end markets are 'highly sensitive to UK interest rates', so the H2 outlook commentary may darken.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior BRCK release turned on a rate decision.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. BRCK's 28 Oct guide explicitly cited 'increased commentators' expectations of interest rate rises', so the hike lands largely inside the guide. Rate-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until the company comments.

findings.finding: Interim dividend decision: last November the Board held the interim at 1.12p while saying it would 'align dividend payments more closely with the prioritisation of debt reduction'. Net debt has since risen to £96.4m (c.2x on the cut guide), so a cut or rebase of the 3.51p total is a live possibility in this release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The dividend has been held at 3.51p (interim 1.12p) through FY25 and FY26, so the stock has never reacted to a cut.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. At 35.3p the 3.51p total is a c.10% trailing yield, which reads as a market expecting a cut; retail commentary on the warning day already called for one. A held interim would be a small positive surprise, a deep cut a negative one; sign uncertain.
findings.independence: Cavendish year-end net debt of c.£86m (1.9x FY27E EBITDA) via https://www.stockopedia.com/content/brck-group-housing-headwinds-cut-earnings-guidance-by-20-as-debt-climbs-we-turn-cautious-1059774/

findings.finding: The H1 net-debt rise from £60.5m to £96.4m, flagged in the domestic retail press as containing c.£16m 'unexplained' outflow, is largely accounted for by public items. These are Jacksons at £15.0m plus freehold property, the 2.39p final dividend paid 25 Sep (c.£7.7m on c.323m shares, derived from Octopus's 51.66m = 15.98% TR-1) and a seasonal H1 working-capital outflow that was £13.5m last year. So the cash-flow line is likely to defuse rather than confirm the bear point.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025 interims carried a £13.5m H1 working-capital outflow and the stock rose 1.54%.
findings.why_not_priced: The only published read of the debt rise (Stockopedia, 28 Oct) calls £16m 'unexplained' and moved its view to AMBER/RED on leverage. Nobody has published the bridge, and the drift since suggests the leverage worry is in the price. This is an inference from public components, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Dividend amount and pay date from the FY26 results: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/brickability-group--brck/final-results/9666643; share count from the Octopus TR-1: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/brickability-group--brck/notification-of-major-holdings-/9827994

findings.finding: The Budget on 28 Oct (the same day as BRCK's warning) confirmed the 'Your First Home' equity-loan scheme: £4.7bn of government lending, c.70,000 households, applications from Feb 2027. BRCK had said it was 'too early to gauge', so the interims are its first chance to comment on the confirmed terms.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measurable; the Nov 2025 interims cited a pending Budget and the stock rose 1.54%.
findings.why_not_priced: The scheme is public and housebuilders have had a month to price it; only BRCK's own read of it is new, and it cannot affect FY27 numbers much because the scheme opens in Feb 2027.

findings.finding: Long holders have been net sellers into and after the warning, with no disclosed buyer. Octopus went from 16.98% to 15.98% on 15 Oct, Alan Simpson sold 3m shares between 25 and 30 Sep, Hanover went from 3.57% to 0% on 18 Sep and Paul Hamilton dropped below 5% on 27 Aug. Post-warning volume stayed elevated (4.75m shares on 16 Nov), and no director bought after the fall.
findings.why_not_priced: The overhang is visible and the drift reflects it. What is not known is whether the seller has finished: no TR-1 has been filed since 16 Oct, so Octopus has not crossed another whole percentage point. An unfinished seller caps a relief bounce; a finished one removes the drag. Sign genuinely uncertain, so sized small.

outside_window.finding: Atlas Holdings' Rule 2.8 six-month lock-out (no-bid statement of 23 Apr 2026, after a rejected 65p proposal) lapsed around 23 Oct 2026. With the stock at 35p, a renewed approach is possible but nothing dated or sourced places one in the window.
'Your First Home' applications open Feb 2027; any volume effect on new-build starts lands in FY28.

baseline_tension: The baseline lean is +1.3 from the -26.5% 20-day run-up, with no short anchor. The findings net to roughly zero (-0.2): a conservative guide and a likely benign cash bridge against a fresh supplier warning, a rate hike and dividend risk. So they neither confirm nor oppose the mean-reversion lean; p_up sits only slightly above 50.
